**Commentary on Surah al-Takathur**, which is Makki according to all the commentators. Al-Bukhari, however, transmitted that it is Madani. It has eight verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.﴾

﴿The mutual rivalry in worldly gain diverts you,﴾ ﴿until you visit the graves.﴾

There are five issues here.

**The first issue:** His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿The mutual rivalry in worldly gain diverts you﴾. *Alhakum* means "preoccupied you." It is said:

*Fa-alhaytuha 'an dhi tama'imin mughayyali*¹

That is, the boastful pursuit of abundance of wealth and number preoccupied you away from obedience to Allah, until you died and were buried in the graves. It is also said that *alhakum* means "made you forget." *Al-takathur* means the act of seeking abundance, of wealth and children. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas and al-Hasan. Qatadah said it means boasting about tribes and clans. al-Dahhak said it means being preoccupied with livelihood and trade.

It is said: *lahiitu 'an kadhā* (with kasra) *alhā luhiyyan wa lihyanan*, when one forgets something, leaves off mentioning it, and turns away from it. *Alhāhu* means "occupied him." *Lahhāhu bihi taljiyatan* means "he diverted him with it," i.e., he kept him occupied with it. *Al-takathur* means *al-mukāthara* (mutual competing in abundance).

Muqatil, Qatadah and others said: it was revealed concerning the Jews when they said, "We are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so, and the sons of so-and-so are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so." That rivalry diverted them until they died in misguidance. Ibn Zayd said it was revealed concerning a clan of the Ansar. Ibn 'Abbas, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said it was revealed concerning two branches of Quraysh: Banu 'Abd Manaf and Banu Sahm. They competed with each other in lordship and nobility in Islam. Each branch said, "We are more numerous in lords, mightier in might, greater in number, and more numerous in protectees." Then Banu 'Abd Manaf outnumbered Banu Sahm. They then competed in the dead, and Banu Sahm outnumbered them in the dead. So it was revealed: ﴿The mutual rivalry in worldly gain diverts you﴾ in your living, ﴿until you visit the graves﴾, boasting of the dead.

Sa'id transmitted from Qatadah that he said: They used to say, "We are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so, and we are greater in number than the sons of so-and-so," while they were dying off day by day, until they all became people of the graves. 'Amr ibn Dinar swore that this surah was revealed concerning merchants. Shaybān transmitted from Qatadah that he said: it was revealed concerning the People of the Book.

I say: the verse encompasses all that has been mentioned and other things besides.

In Sahih Muslim, from Mutarrif, from his father, who said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was reciting ﴿The mutual rivalry in worldly gain diverts you﴾. He said: "The son of Adam says, 'My wealth, my wealth!' Yet what is yours of your wealth, O son of Adam, except what you eat and so consume, or what you wear and so wear out, or what you give in charity and so send ahead? [And what is other than that will go away and be left for people.]"²

Al-Bukhari transmitted from Ibn Shihab: Anas ibn Malik informed me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If the son of Adam had a valley of gold, he would love to have two valleys. Nothing will fill his mouth except dust, and Allah turns in forgiveness to whoever repents." Thabit transmitted from Anas, from Ubayy, who said: "We used to regard this as part of the Qur'an, until ﴿The mutual rivalry in worldly gain diverts you﴾ was revealed."

Ibn al-'Arabi said: this is a sound and excellent text. It escaped the people of tafsir, so they erred and were ignorant. Praise be to Allah for knowledge.

Ibn 'Abbas said: the Prophet ﷺ recited ﴿The mutual rivalry in worldly gain diverts you﴾ and said: "The abundance of wealth is gathering it from other than its rightful source, withholding it from its rightful due, and tying it up in containers."

**The second issue:** His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿until you visit the graves﴾. That is, until death came to you, and you became visitors in the graves, returning from them as a visitor returns to his dwelling, either to Paradise or to Hell. It is said of one who has died: "He has visited his grave." It is also said that the meaning is: the rivalry diverted you until you counted the dead, as already mentioned. It is also said that this is a warning: you were preoccupied with boasting about this world until you visited the graves, and then you will see what the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will bring upon you.

**The third issue:** His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿the graves﴾. *Al-maqābir* is the plural of *maqbara* and *maqbura* (with fatha and damma on the ba'). *Al-qubūr* is the plural of *qabr* (grave). A poet said:

*Ara ahla al-qusuri idha umituu...*
*banaw fawqa al-maqabiri bi-al-sukhuuri*

*Abaw illa mubahatan wa fakhran*
*'ala al-fuqara'i hatta fi al-qubuuri*

The word *al-maqbar* also occurs in poetry. He said:

*Li-kulli unasin maqbarun bi-finā'ihim*
*fahum yanqusuuna wa al-qubuuru tazīdu*³

*Al-Maqburi* and *al-Maqbari* are attributed to Abu Sa'id al-Maqburi, who used to live in the graveyards. *Qabartu al-mayyit* means "I buried the dead," *aqbartuhu* means "I ordered that he be buried." The discussion of this was already mentioned in Surah 'Abasa.⁴ And praise be to Allah.

**The fourth issue:** The word *al-maqābir* (graves) is not mentioned in revelation except in this surah. Visiting graves is among the greatest remedies for a hard heart, because it reminds one of death and the Hereafter. That leads to shortness of hope, asceticism toward this world, and abandoning desire for it.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "I had forbidden you to visit the graves; so visit the graves, for they make one ascetic toward this world and remind one of the Hereafter." Ibn Mas'ud transmitted it, and Ibn Majah recorded it. In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: "for it reminds one of death." In al-Tirmidhi, from Buraydah: "for it reminds one of the Hereafter." He said: this is a good, sound hadith. Also in it, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed women who visit graves. He said: and in the chapter there are reports from Ibn 'Abbas and Hassan ibn Thabit. Abu 'Isa said: this is a good, sound hadith.

Some scholars held that this prohibition was before the Prophet ﷺ permitted visiting graves, and when he permitted it, both men and women entered that permission. Some said that he disliked women visiting graves because of their lack of patience and their excessive grief.

I say: visiting graves for men is agreed upon among the scholars, while for women it is disputed. As for young women, it is forbidden for them to go out; as for older women past childbearing, it is permissible for them. It is allowed for all of them when they go out alone without men. There is no dispute about this, if Allah wills. On this meaning, the saying ﴿visit the graves﴾ is general. As for a place or a time in which temptation is feared from the gathering of men and women, it is not lawful and not permissible.

For while a man goes out to take a lesson, his gaze falls upon a woman and he is tempted; and conversely, so each of the men and women returns burdened with sin, not rewarded. And Allah knows best.

**The fifth issue:** The scholars said: whoever wishes to treat his heart and to bring it under the chains of subjugation to obey his Lord should frequently remember the destroyer of pleasures,⁵ the separator of communities, the one who orphans sons and daughters. He should be constant in witnessing the dying and in visiting the graves of deceased Muslims. These are three matters that whoever has a hardened heart and is burdened by sin should use as a remedy for his disease and seek help from against the temptations of Satan and his helpers. If he benefits from frequent remembrance of death and the hardness of his heart is cleared away by it, well and good. But if the rust on his heart is great and the motives of sin are firmly established in him, then witnessing the dying and visiting the graves of deceased Muslims reaches further in removing that than the first, because the remembrance of death is informing the heart of what it will come to, and it stands in place of fear and warning. In witnessing one who is dying and in visiting the grave of one who has died among the Muslims there is direct observation and witnessing, and therefore it is more effective than the first. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The report is not like direct observation," narrated by Ibn 'Abbas.

As for taking a lesson from the condition of the dying, that is not possible at all times, and it may not happen to one who wishes to treat his heart at some hour. As for visiting graves, its availability is quicker, and benefiting from it is more fitting and more suitable. So whoever resolves to visit should adopt its etiquette, bring his heart present in going to it, and not make his share from it merely wandering among the tombs, for this is a state in which a beast shares with him. We seek refuge in Allah from that. Rather, he should intend by his visit the face of Allah, Exalted, and the reform of the corruption of his heart, or benefit to the dead by reciting the Qur'an and supplicating for him there. He should avoid walking on the graves and sitting upon them. When he enters the graveyard he should greet its people, and when he reaches the grave of his deceased whom he knows, he should greet him as well, and face him directly, for in his visit he is like one speaking to him while he is alive. If he were speaking to him while alive, the proper etiquette would be to face him, so likewise here.

Then he should take a lesson from one who has gone beneath the dust and has been cut off from family and loved ones, after having led armies and troops, competed with companions and clans, and gathered wealth and treasures. Death came to him at a time he did not expect and a terror he did not anticipate. So let the visitor reflect on the condition of those of his brothers who have passed away, and those of his peers who have departed, who attained their hopes and gathered wealth: how their hopes were cut off, how their wealth did not avail them, how the dust erased the beauty of their faces, how their parts were scattered in the graves, how their women became widowed after them, how the humiliation of orphanhood encompassed their children, and how others divided their old and new possessions.

And let him remember their going back and forth in their aims, their eagerness to attain their goals, their being deceived by the arrangement of circumstances, and their reliance on health and youth. Let him know that his inclination toward play and sport is like their inclination, and his heedlessness of the terrible death and swift destruction that lie before him is like their heedlessness, and that he will inevitably arrive at their destination. Let him bring to his heart the remembrance of one who used to go back and forth in his purposes, and how his legs were broken, and who used to delight in looking at what had been granted to him while his eyes ran with tears; who used to boast with the eloquence of his speech while worms had eaten his tongue; who used to laugh at the fortunes of his time while dust had worn away his teeth. Let him be certain that his state is like their state and his end is like their end.

At this remembrance and reflection, all worldly preoccupations depart from him, and he turns to the works of the Hereafter. He becomes ascetic toward his worldly life, turns to obedience to his Master, his heart softens, and his limbs become humble.

We have mentioned in the book "al-Tadhkirah" that belief in it is obligatory and affirming it is necessary, as the Truthful One (ﷺ) informed, and that Allah the Exalted restores life to the accountable servant in his grave, by returning life to him, and gives him reason in the same manner in which he lived, so that he understands what he is asked about and what he answers, and comprehends what has come to him from his Lord and what has been prepared for him in his grave of honour or humiliation. This is the position of the People of the Sunnah and what the community of the People of the Religion holds. We have discussed it there in full, and praise be to Allah. It was also said: "Nay, you will come to know" at the raising of the dead that you will be resurrected; "then, nay, you will come to know" on the Day of Resurrection that you will be punished. On this view the states of the Resurrection are included, from resurrection and gathering, questioning and presentation, to its other terrors and frights, as we have mentioned in the book "al-Tadhkirah, on the States of the Dead and the Matters of the Hereafter." Al-Dahhak said: "Nay, you will come to know" refers to the disbelievers, and "then, nay, you will come to know": the believers say [this]. Thus he used to recite it: the first with the letter ta' (you), and the second with the letter ya' (they).

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 102, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nay, if you knew with certainty of certainty﴾. He repeated "kalla" (nay), which is a rebuke and an admonition, because He follows each one with something else, as if He said: "Do not do it, for you will regret it; do not do it, for you will deserve punishment." The idafa (genitive construction) of "knowledge" to "certainty" is like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, this is the truth of certainty﴾ [[Qur'an 56:95.]] [al-Waqi'ah: 95]. It has been said that "al-yaqin" here means death, as stated by Qatadah. It is also reported from him that it means the Resurrection, because when it comes, doubt vanishes; that is, "if you knew with the knowledge of the Resurrection." The response of "law" (if) is omitted, meaning: if you knew today about the Resurrection what you will know when the Trumpet is blown, and the graves are split open over your corpses, and how your gathering will be, that would occupy you away from competing in worldly accumulation. It has also been said: "Nay, if you knew with certainty of certainty," meaning, if [[So in the manuscripts of the original.]] the scrolls had already flown open, then there would be the wretched and the happy.

It has been said that "kalla" in these three places has the meaning of "alla" (verily/indeed), as stated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Al-Farra' said it has the meaning of "haqqan" (truly). The discussion of it has already been treated comprehensively [[See vol. 11, p. 147 and following.]].

"His saying, the Exalted: ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire﴾. This is another warning. It is with an implied oath, meaning: you will surely see the Hellfire in the Hereafter. The address is to the disbelievers for whom the Fire is obligatory. It has also been said that it is general, as He said: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾ [Maryam 19:71], so the Fire is a dwelling for the disbelievers and a passage for the believers. In the Sahih (it is reported): "Then the first of them will pass like lightning, then like the wind, then like a bird..." and the hadith continues. It has already been discussed in Surah Maryam [see vol. 11, p. 137]. Al-Kisa'i and Ibn 'Amir read ﴿latarawunna﴾ with a dammah on the ta', from "aratuhu al-shay'" (I showed him the thing), meaning: you will be gathered toward it and you will see it. With a fatha on the ta', which is the reading of the majority, it means: you will surely see the Hellfire with your eyes from a distance.

﴿Then you will surely see it with the certainty of sight﴾: that is, direct witnessing. It has also been said that this is a report of the continuance of their stay in the Fire, meaning the seeing is constant and uninterrupted, and the address on this view is to the disbelievers. It has also been said that the meaning of ﴿If you knew with the certainty of knowledge﴾ is: if you knew today in this world with the certainty of knowledge what lies before you, of what I have described, you would see the Hellfire with the eyes of your hearts, for the certainty of knowledge shows you the Hellfire with the eye of your heart, which is that the events of the Resurrection and the crossing of its stages are pictured for you. Then ﴿you will surely see it with the certainty of sight﴾: that is, at the moment of direct witnessing with the eye of the head, so you will see it as certainty, it will not be absent from your eye. Then ﴿you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾: at the place of questioning and presentation."

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 102, verse 8:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the bounty.﴾ Muslim related in his Sahih from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out one day, or one night, and found Abu Bakr and Umar. He said: ("What brought you out of your houses at this hour?") They said: "Hunger, O Messenger of Allah." He said: ("By Him in whose hand is my soul, what brought you out is what brought me out. Stand up.") So they stood up with him, and he came to a man of the Ansar, but he was not in his house. When his wife saw him, she said: "Welcome and well come." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: ("Where is so-and-so?") She said: "He has gone to fetch sweet water for us." Then the Ansari came, looked at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his two companions, and said: "Praise be to Allah! No one has been more honoured in his guests today than I have." He said: So he set off and brought them a bunch of dates containing unripe, ripe and fully ripe dates, and said: "Eat from these." He took a knife, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: ("Beware of the milk-giver.") So he slaughtered for them, and they ate from the sheep and from that bunch, and drank. When they were full and satisfied, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abu Bakr and Umar: ("By Him in whose hand is my soul, you will surely be asked about the bounty of this day on the Day of Resurrection: hunger brought you out of your houses, and you did not return until this bounty befell you.") Al-Tirmidhi transmitted it, and he said in it: ("This, by Him in whose hand is my soul, is part of the bounty about which you will be asked on the Day of Resurrection: cool shade, good ripe dates, and cold water.") The man of the Ansar was given the kunya Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayhan, and he (the narrator) mentioned his story. I say: The name of this Ansari man is Malik ibn al-Tayhan, and he is known by the kunya Abu al-Haytham. In connection with this story, Abdullah ibn Rawahah says, praising Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayhan:

I have not seen, like Islam, a might for a community,
nor like the guests of al-Irashi [[As in all copies of the original.]] a company.

A Prophet, a truthful one, and the Faruq of the community,
and the best of the sons of Hawwa in branch and origin.

They met at an appointed time and a decreed matter,
and Allah's decree was a determined destiny [[In a copy of the original: "a command."]].

To a Najdi man who competes in his generosity
with the suns of forenoon in generosity, glory and pride,

And the horseman of Allah's creation in every raid,
when the people don their iron coats of mail, riveted.

So he ransomed and welcomed them, then brought near their hospitality,
and gave them nothing but fat, dates-steeped [[The end of the poem.]].

Abu Nu'aym al-Hafiz also mentioned, from Abu Asib, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us at night, and I went out to him. Then he passed by Abu Bakr and called him, and he came out to him. Then he passed by Umar and called him, and he came out to him. He went on until he entered a garden of one of the Ansar. He said to the owner of the garden: ("Feed us some unripe dates.") So he brought a bunch, placed it down, and they ate. Then he called for water and drank, and said: ("You will surely be asked about this on the Day of Resurrection.") He said: Umar took the bunch and struck it against the ground until the unripe dates scattered toward the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we really be asked about this on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: ("Yes, except for three things: a morsel with which one stills his hunger, a garment with which one covers his nakedness, or a shelter in which one takes refuge from heat and cold.")

The scholars of interpretation differed about the bounty about which one will be asked, into ten opinions. The first: security and health, said by Ibn Mas'ud. The second: health and leisure, said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr. In Bukhari, from him (peace be upon him): ("Two blessings in which many people are cheated: health and leisure.") [[That is, they are at a loss in them. Ni'mah (blessing) is what a person enjoys and finds pleasant. Ghabn (cheating) is buying for many times the price, or selling for less than the market value. So whoever has a sound body and is free from preoccupations that hinder him, yet does not strive for the good of his Hereafter, is like one who is cheated in a sale. The purpose is to show that most people do not benefit from health and leisure, but spend them in other than their proper places. (From the commentary on Sunan Ibn Majah.)]] The third: perception through the faculties of hearing and sight, said by Ibn Abbas. In the Revelation: ﴿Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart, all of those will be asked about.﴾ [[Verse 36 of Surah al-Isra'.]] [al-Isra': 36]. In the Sahih, from Abu Hurairah and Abu Sa'id, who both said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ("A servant will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and He will say to him: Did I not make for you hearing and sight, and wealth and children...") the hadith. Al-Tirmidhi transmitted it and said in it: a good, sound hadith. The fourth: the pleasure of food and drink, said by Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari. The hadith of Abu Hurairah indicates this. The fifth: that it is lunch and dinner, said by al-Hasan. The sixth: the saying of Makhul al-Shami: that it is the fullness of bellies, cold drink, shade of dwellings, soundness of physique, and the pleasure of sleep. Zayd ibn Aslam related it from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ("You will surely be asked about the bounty on that day") meaning about the fullness of bellies... (. He was then mentioned. Al-Mawardi mentioned it and said: This question includes both the disbeliever and the believer, except that the believer's question is glad tidings that the bounty of this world and the bounty of the Hereafter will be combined for him, while the disbeliever's question is rebuke, because he met the bounty of this world with disbelief and disobedience. Some people said: This question about every blessing applies only to disbelievers. It is related that when this verse was revealed, Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of a meal I ate with you in the house of Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayhan, of barley bread, meat, unripe dates that had begun to ripen, and sweet water? Do we fear that this is part of the bounty about which we will be asked?" He (peace be upon him) said: ("That is for the disbelievers,") then he recited: ﴿And do We reward any but the ungrateful?﴾ [[Verse 17 of Surah Saba'. This is the reading of Nafi'.]] [Saba': 17]. This was mentioned by al-Qushayri Abu Nasr. Al-Hasan said: None will be asked about the bounty except the people of the Fire. Al-Qushayri said: The reconciliation of the reports is that all will be asked, but the question to the disbelievers is a rebuke, because they abandoned gratitude, while the question to the believer is a question of honour, because he was grateful. And this bounty is in every blessing. I say: This view is good, because the wording is general. Al-Firyabi mentioned: Warqa' related to us from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the bounty﴾, he said: everything of the pleasure of this world. Abu al-Ahwas related from Abdullah, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: ("Allah, Exalted is He, will enumerate His blessings upon the servant on the Day of Resurrection, until He counts for him: You asked Me for so-and-so woman to marry you, so I named her by her name and married her to you.") In al-Tirmidhi, from Abu Hurairah, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the bounty﴾, the people said: "O Messenger of Allah, about which bounty are we asked? For there are only the two blacks [[Al-aswadan: the dates and the water.]], and the enemy is present, and our swords are on our shoulders." He said: ("That will indeed come about.") And from him, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ("The first thing a servant will be asked about on the Day of Resurrection, meaning the servant, is that it will be said to him: Did We not make your body healthy, and quench you with cold water?") He said: From the hadith of Ibn Umar, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: ("When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will call one of His servants, make him stand before Him, and ask him about his status just as He asks him about his wealth.") Status is certainly among the bounties of this world. Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said: it is health of the body and contentment of the soul. This is the seventh opinion. It was also said: sleep together with security and well-being. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: What satisfies hunger and covers nakedness of coarse food and clothing, a person will not be asked about it on the Day of Resurrection; he will only be asked about the bounty. He said: The evidence for this is that Allah, Exalted is He, settled Adam in the Garden and said to him: ﴿Indeed, it is [granted] for you that you will not go hungry therein or be unclothed, and that you will not be thirsty therein or be exposed to the sun.﴾ [[Verses 118 and 119 of Surah Ta-Ha.]] [Ta-Ha: 118-119]. So these four things, what stills hunger, what drives away thirst, what shelters from heat, and what covers nakedness, were for Adam, peace be upon him, absolutely, with no reckoning for them, because he had no escape from them. I say: Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr mentioned something similar, saying: Among what the servant will not be asked about is clothing that covers his nakedness, food that keeps his back upright, and a place that shelters him from heat and cold. I say: This is drawn from his saying, peace be upon him: ("The son of Adam has no right in anything beyond these qualities: a house in which he dwells, a garment that covers his nakedness, and plain bread and water.") Al-Tirmidhi transmitted it. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: Plain bread means there is no condiment with it. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: The bounty is what Allah has bestowed upon us through Muhammad ﷺ. In the Revelation: ﴿Allah has certainly conferred a favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from among themselves.﴾ [[Verse 164 of Surah Al 'Imran.]] [Al 'Imran: 164]. Al-Hasan also, and al-Mufaddal, said: it is the lightening of the laws and the facilitation of the Qur'an. Allah says: ﴿And He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship.﴾ [[Verse 78 of Surah al-Hajj.]] [al-Hajj: 78], and He says: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [[Verse 17 of Surah al-Qamar.]] [al-Qamar: 17]. I say: All of these are blessings, and the servant will be asked about them: whether he gave thanks for them or disbelieved. The earlier opinions are more apparent. And Allah knows best.
